title: Bead oscillating in water: unsteady Stokes drag vs frequency (frequency response, mixed u-p, analytic)
description:
Optical-tweezer calibration geometry: a polystyrene bead of radius a = 1 um (E 3.5 GPa, nu 0.34, rho_b 1050 kg/m^3) held by prescribed_displacement_domain 'bead' and moved along the axis by X = 1 nm in library water (viscosity mu = 1.002e-3 Pa s, rho = 998.2 kg/m^3, no bulk modulus: an incompressible viscous liquid), axisymmetric (r, z) with the bead centre on the axis at z = 50 um, the container r < 50 um, 0 < z < 100 um with fixed walls (x_lo is the axis). solid_mechanics on quadratic triangles (h = 0.12 um inside the bead, growth 1.25, 2.5 um at most), formulation mixed (Taylor-Hood: P2 displacement, P1 pressure per material), frequency_response at 8 log-spaced frequencies from 10 kHz to 1 MHz: a / delta = sqrt(f / f_nu) from 0.18 to 1.8 (delta = sqrt(2 mu / (rho omega)) the viscous penetration depth, f_nu = mu / (pi rho a^2) = 319 kHz); the container is at least 8.8 delta away, so the wall corrections (exp(-(R - a) / delta) and (a / R)^3) stay below 1e-3.
Analytic (Stokes 1851, Landau-Lifshitz section 24; exp(+j omega t), U = j omega X, lam = sqrt(j omega rho / mu) = (1 + j) / delta): the force of the water on the bead F = -6 pi mu a U (1 + lam a + lam^2 a^2 / 9) = 6 pi mu a omega X (s + 2 s^2 / 9) - j 6 pi mu a omega X (1 + s), s = a / delta (the lam^2 term is the added mass of half the displaced water). The reaction table of 'bead' is the force the support exerts on the bead, which also accelerates the bead itself: F_y = -F - omega^2 m_b X, m_b = rho_b 4/3 pi a^3.
Curves & tables tab: the bead reaction F_y_re (drag in quadrature with the motion plus the inertia of bead and added mass) and F_y_im (the dissipative drag 6 pi mu a omega X (1 + sqrt(f / f_nu))) versus frequency with their analytic curves; the derived curve drag_ratio_vs_stokes = Im F / (6 pi mu a omega X (1 + sqrt(f / f_nu))), the frequency-dependent drag correction a tweezer calibration applies to the Stokes gamma_0, over the analytic 1 (per row of the table, low to high frequency). Derived values tab: the drag ratio Im F / (6 pi mu a omega X) at 10 kHz and 1 MHz against 1 + sqrt(f / f_nu). Field tab: u_abs and the pressure (p > 0 in compression) of the last frequency. Expected agreement (measured, relative; P2 / P1 with ~4.7 elements per delta at 1 MHz): drag ratio 1.0e-4 at 10 kHz and 5.4e-5 at 1 MHz, curve errors F_y_re 2.6e-5 and F_y_im 5.4e-5, drag_ratio_vs_stokes 1.1e-4 (3.2 s); tolerances 4e-4, 2e-4, 1e-4, 2e-4 and 4e-4 (~3.7 x measured).
